record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.context_brief: On-chain proxy variables for nominal anchors
record.original_question: If secure permissionless oracles for arbitrary external data are impossible, can on-chain proxy variables such as mining hash rate, block timing, or mining difficulty serve as viable nominal-anchor proxies for stablecoins, and are such proxies incentive-compatible, hard to game, and secure?

evidence.quote:
It is
possible that secure permissionless oracles for arbitrary data
are a theoretical impossibility [7]. In such a case, a ﬁnal
possibility for the realization of completely permissionless
stablecoins remains in the deepened investigation of on-chain
proxy variables for relevant nominal anchors like current
prices. We are currently aware only of the current mining hash
rate, as materialized, e.g., in the timing between blocks and the
current mining difﬁculty, as a potentially viable representative
of this class. More research is needed here to further test the
viability of this approach, especially in respect to incentive-
compatibility, gameability and security (c.f. Sec. V-E).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a permissionless proof-of-work blockchain that supports a stablecoin protocol. A stablecoin requires a nominal anchor — a reference signal (typically tied to an external price level) that the protocol can use to adjust supply or collateral parameters so that the coin's value remains stable. Suppose that secure permissionless oracles for arbitrary off-chain data (such as exchange rates) are unavailable, so the protocol may only use information that is verifiable on-chain (purely endogenous quantities such as the sequence of block timestamps, block headers, transaction data, the current mining difficulty target, and the inferred mining hash rate).

Define an on-chain proxy variable to be a function P: (chain history up to height h) → ℝ computable by any full node. Call such a proxy a viable nominal-anchor proxy if it satisfies all of the following:

(i) Informativeness: P is statistically correlated with an external nominal anchor (e.g. the purchasing power or fiat price of the native coin) strongly enough that a control rule based on P can keep the stablecoin's market value within a bounded band around its target with high probability under normal economic conditions.

(ii) Incentive compatibility: in the game where miners and users choose strategies to maximize expected profit, honest participation (truthful block production at the natural difficulty) remains a (sub-game-perfect) equilibrium when the stablecoin protocol consumes P.

(iii) Non-gameability: there is no coalition of miners and/or users controlling less than some threshold α < 1/2 of hash power and bounded capital that can profitably manipulate P away from its honest value by more than ε, for specified small ε > 0.

(iv) Security: the protocol built on P does not introduce new attack vectors that reduce the consensus security of the underlying blockchain.

Question: Does there exist an on-chain proxy variable P — for instance one constructed from the mining hash rate, inter-block timing, or the mining difficulty — that is a viable nominal-anchor proxy in the sense above? Equivalently, exhibit such a P together with a proof that it satisfies (i)–(iv), or prove that no function of purely on-chain data can simultaneously satisfy (i)–(iv).
artifact.status_search_result: No formal resolution was found. The question of whether purely on-chain proxies (hash rate, block timing, difficulty) can serve as incentive-compatible, non-gameable nominal anchors for permissionless stablecoins remains an open research problem; subsequent stablecoin literature continues to rely either on collateralization with off-chain price oracles or on algorithmic mechanisms whose stability is empirically fragile, without producing a proxy proven to satisfy the stated criteria.

status_evidence.title: SoK: Stablecoins (Clark, Demirag, Moosavi)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys stablecoin designs and notes that fully permissionless, oracle-free stablecoins remain unrealized; on-chain endogenous signals have not been shown to provide viable nominal anchors.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of finding a viable, incentive-compatible on-chain nominal-anchor proxy is still considered open in the stablecoin literature.

status_evidence.title: Decentralized Stablecoin Design (survey literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews monetary-policy mechanisms for cryptocurrencies and identifies the lack of trustworthy endogenous proxies for external nominal anchors as an unresolved obstacle.
status_evidence.claim: No construction is known that provably satisfies informativeness, incentive compatibility, non-gameability, and security simultaneously using only on-chain data.
